backlog.title: Pre-compute Featurization

backlog.spec: Change MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 1.0. This allows the Random Forest to use all available features (Morgan bits + descriptors) at every split. Since the dataset is small (728 molecules), a lower feature fraction might be restricting the model's ability to find important signal in the dense fingerprint space.
backlog.title: Increase max_features to 1.0

backlog.spec: In addition to the Morgan fingerprint and descriptors, calculate and append RDKit MACCS keys (2048 bits) to the feature vector. This provides a different view of molecular structure (pre-defined substructures) compared to the circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Append RDKit Descriptors.MolWt(mol) and the sum of partial charges (or formal charges) to the feature list. Molecular weight is a very common descriptor in drug-likeness and permeability tasks.

backlog.spec: Standardize the training targets (train_y) using sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler before fitting the RandomForestRegressor, and apply the same transformation to the test set. This can help the regressor converge or find better patterns if the distribution is skewed.

backlog.spec: Introduce regularization to the RandomForestRegressor by setting `min_samples_split=5` and `min_samples_leaf=2`. This helps prevent the trees from overfitting to the noise in the small 728-molecule dataset.
backlog.title: Random Forest with Min Samples Split/Leaf constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of using `gen.GetFingerprintAsNumPy(mol)` which returns a bit vector, consider if using a count-based approach (if supported by the generator) or simply ensuring the bits are treated as a high-dimensional sparse-like space would improve the RF's ability to weight bit occurrence.
backlog.title: Use Quantized/Count-based Morgan Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Apply sklearn.preprocessing.RobustScaler to the featurized numpy array before passing it to the RandomForestRegressor. This handles outliers in the descriptor values (like LogP or TPSA) which might otherwise dominate the splits.
backlog.title: Robust Scaler on Features

backlog.title: Add RDKit PhysChem Descriptors

backlog.title: Reduce MAX_FEATURES

backlog.title: Switch to XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace `RandomForestRegressor` with `lightgbm.LGBMRegressor`. Use `n_estimators=500`, `learning_rate=0.1`, `num_leaves=31`, `random_state=seed`, and `n_jobs=-1`.
backlog.title: Switch to LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace `RandomForestRegressor` with `catboost.CatBoostRegressor`. Use `iterations=1000`, `learning_rate=0.1`, `depth=6`, `random_state=seed`, and `logging_level='Silent'`.
backlog.title: Switch to CatBoost

backlog.spec: Change the `RADIUS` constant from 2 to 3. This captures larger local chemical environments in the Morgan fingerprint.
backlog.title: Radius 3 Morgan Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add RDKit's Atom Pair fingerprints to the feature set. These fingerprints encode the distance between pairs of atoms, capturing long-range structural information that Morgan fingerprints (radius 2) might miss. Concatenate them with the existing Morgan, MACCS, and descriptor features.
backlog.title: Atom Pair Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan fingerprints with RDKit's Topological Torsion fingerprints. These are designed to capture the 3D-like connectivity of the molecule's skeleton and might provide better structural descriptors for permeability prediction than 2D circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: Topological Torsion Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Instead of selecting specific descriptors (LogP, TPSA, etc.), use the full set of RDKit's 200+ physical-chemical descriptors. Calculate them for each molecule and concatenate them with the Morgan and MACCS fingerprints.
backlog.title: Full RDKit Descriptor Set

backlog.spec: Implement a simple ensemble by training 5 separate RandomForestRegressor models, each with a different random seed (e.g., seed, seed+1, seed+2, etc.). The final prediction for the test set should be the median of the 5 models' predictions. This helps reduce variance and improve stability.
backlog.title: Ensemble: Median of 5 RFs

backlog.spec: Calculate the Molecular Weight (MW) for every molecule in the training set. Use the inverse of the MW (1/MW) as the sample weight during the RandomForestRegressor.fit() call. This may help the model prioritize smaller molecules which often have different permeability profiles.
backlog.title: Weighted Fit by Molecular Weight

backlog.spec: Calculate the mean of the training target y. Subtract this mean from all training y values and all test predictions, then add it back to the final predictions. While Random Forest is invariant to linear shifts, this can sometimes improve numerical stability during the splitting process.
backlog.title: Target Mean Offset

backlog.spec: Use the 'class_weight' equivalent for regression by identifying the distribution of the target y. Since we want to minimize MAE, identify the most frequent 20% range of target values and oversample those instances (or use a weight vector) to ensure the model doesn't ignore lower or higher permeability outliers.
backlog.title: Balanced Forest for Imbalanced Distribution

backlog.spec: Set max_samples=0.8 in the RandomForestRegressor. This forces each tree to be trained on a different bootstrap sample of the data (80% of the total), increasing the diversity of the individual trees and potentially lowering the test error.
backlog.title: Subsample for Variance Reduction

backlog.spec: Use RDKit to calculate the 'Principal Moments of Inertia' (PMI) for each molecule. These three values provide a signature of the molecule's shape (elongated vs spherical) and can be added as three extra columns to the feature matrix.
backlog.title: Coordinate/Conformer-Independent 3D Features

backlog.spec: For each molecule, generate the Morgan fingerprints of its fragments (e.g., rings and side chains) separately and concatenate these as additional features. This helps the model recognize common functional groups in different environments.
backlog.title: Recursive Featurization

incumbent.description: Append RDKit MACCS keys (167 bits, since MACCS is a fixed-length 167-bit key set and has no 2048-bit form) to the existing Morgan fingerprint and descriptor features for the random forest.

memo:
Helped: cheap physchem and keys features added to Morgan+RF. HBD/HBA counts gave the biggest gain (slot 6, 0.3979, -0.0347). Crippen logP/TPSA/rotatable bonds (slot 15, 0.3914/0.3857) and MACCS keys (slot 25, 0.3839/0.3807) were also accepted. Incumbent: mean_adjusted 0.3823 over 2 runs.
Did not help: model swaps (XGBoost 0.4770, LightGBM 0.4244, CatBoost 0.4077, ExtraTrees 0.3853 on the latest run), forest regularization (max_depth 10 at 0.4078, max_samples 0.8 at 0.3868), sample weighting (0.3969, 0.4001), Morgan radius 3, 1024/4096 bits (0.3976, 0.3850), count Morgan (0.3923), MolWt/charge (0.3917), aromatic ring count (0.3853). Many aborts were repeats or about models train.py lacks.
Next: stay with the RF. Try other fingerprints beside MACCS (atom-pair, topological torsion, RDKit FP), the full RDKit descriptor set, and a blend of RF with a different model. Check the list above before proposing, to avoid repeats.
